After I worked on Do My Laundry, the CEO asked if I could work on a React/.NET project. I took on the challenge and got onboarded with a new team, this time working with more engineers and a larger project scope.

I learned here, the hard way, that using Claude and Copilot tools doesn’t always mean reliable and efficient code. Not everything that the AI-assisted tool could generate is of quality. So we need to read the code manually and ensure that it follows the team coding styles and conventions.
problems_encountered: When I first worked on the application, the data forms and landing pages were working very slow so it took me a lot of time to load the pages and debug the features.

There is a lot to setup at first—the backend code and frontend code as well as the test data—so getting up to speed with the onboarding took a bit of time. There were also passwords and credentials that I need to have access with and the night shift difference made the onboarding flow slow.
When I first worked on a big feature, I wasn't fully aware of the coding styles and conventions of the team, so I experienced a bit of hiccup there.

All in all, after I first pushed and developed my first feature or fixes for the project, after I got onboarded and got familiar with the coding styles and conventions of the team, I had a breeze with working on the next features and bugfixes.
